question: Which of the following reactions represents symbolic combination reaction?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Option - 2.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****__Combination Reaction-__ **

__
 
• A direct combination reaction is a reaction where two or more elements or compounds combine to form a single compound.
 
• Such reactions are represented by equations of the following form:** A + B → C.**
 
• In combination reactions, there is no limitation in the number of reactants that can participate in the reaction. Also, the reaction is generally** exothermic because, during a combination reaction, a new bond is formed between the reactant molecules that lead to the release of heat.**
 
• ***For example,***
 
• The formation of the **salt barium fluoride **by the combination of **barium metal **and **fluorine gas **is a highly exothermic reaction.
 
• **Ba (s) + F2 (g) → BaF2 (s)**

**Types of Combination Reactions**__

There are 3 ways in which a combination reaction can take place.

__
 
• ***Combination of two or more elements-***.
 
• Carbon and oxygen combine to form Carbon Dioxide gas
 
• **C (g) + O2 (g) → CO2 (g)**
 
• ***Combination of two or more compounds -***
 
• The formation of calcium hydroxide (slaked lime) by the reaction of calcium oxide (quick lime) and water.
 
• CaO (s) + H2O(l) → Ca(OH)2 (s)
 
• ***Combination of compound with element -***
 
• Formation of Carbon Dioxide gas from the compound carbon monoxide and the element oxygen is an example of this type of combination reaction
 
• 2 CO(g) + O2 (g) → 2 CO2 (g)​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__***Some other types of Reaction - ***__

 
 

 **Type of chemical reaction **
 **Explanation**
 **General representation**
 
 

 ***Decomposition reaction***
 The opposite of a combination reaction – a complex molecule breaks down to make simpler ones.
 **AB → A + B**
 
 

 ***Precipitation reaction***
 Two solutions of soluble salts are mixed resulting in an insoluble solid (precipitate) forming.
 **A + Soluble salt B → Precipitate + soluble salt C**
 
 

 ***Displacement reaction***
 One element takes place with another element in the compound.
 **A + BC → AC + B**
